issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle you can find, a sweet smell, the engine running hot, or milky, light-brown sludge on the oil cap or dipstick.
issues.why: The plastic-framed lower intake gaskets on the 3.8L V6 break down and leak coolant, either outside the engine or into the oil. GM issued several bulletins on these leaks and on coolant getting into the oil.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and look at the oil for a milky color. If coolant is in the oil, stop driving it until the gaskets are replaced and the oil is changed, because coolant ruins the engine bearings.

issues.t: Cracked plastic upper intake manifold
issues.sym: Coolant leaking from the top of the engine near the throttle body, a sweet smell, overheating, or a sudden loss of coolant.
issues.why: The upper intake on the non-supercharged 3.8L is plastic and carries coolant. It cracks with heat and age, and on some cars the leak led to overheating and engine damage. GM released new upper intake and gasket kits.
issues.next: Stop and let the engine cool if the temperature gauge rises. Have the upper intake checked; the improved replacement part with new gaskets is the fix.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails or won't go into gear
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between shifts, no drive or no reverse, or the car not moving at all when put in gear.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears internally with age and mileage. Transmission failure is one of the most-reported Bonneville problems, often around 90,000–130,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't engage, avoid driving it and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or replacement is usually needed.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic shifting
issues.sym: Hard, banging shifts, flaring between gears, erratic shift timing, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: GM bulletins tie these symptoms to the transmission's pressure control solenoid, which controls how firmly the gears apply.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read and the fluid checked. Replacing the solenoid can fix it before more damage is done.

issues.t: Power window drops into the door or stops working
issues.sym: A window falls down into the door, goes up crooked, makes a grinding or popping noise, or the motor runs but the glass does not move.
issues.why: The window regulator's cable and plastic parts break. This is the most-reported Bonneville complaint, especially for 2000 to 2002, and GM issued a bulletin for windows that are noisy, stop working or drop.
issues.next: Tape or prop the glass up to keep rain out until it is repaired. Usually only the regulator needs replacing.

issues.t: Water leaks into the car or trunk
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front or rear floor, water in the trunk, a musty smell, or fogged windows after rain.
issues.why: Water gets past body seals and seams. GM issued bulletins for floor leaks, trunk leaks and leaks around the lamps.
issues.next: Note where the water shows up after rain or a car wash and have a body shop water-test the car. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Engine stalls or surges while driving
issues.sym: The engine surges, loses power, or shuts off while driving or at idle, then may restart after a few minutes.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor or mass airflow sensor is the most common cause reported on these cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Stalling in traffic is dangerous, so get it checked soon. A shop can test the sensors; replacing the failed sensor is usually a straightforward fix.

issues.t: Car won't start or starts only sometimes
issues.sym: The engine won't crank, or it cranks but doesn't start, on and off with no clear pattern.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for intermittent no-start and no-crank problems traced to the ignition/start switch and to low charging voltage. Owners also report no-start repairs on older models.
issues.next: Note whether the engine cranks and whether the security light flashes when it fails. Have the battery, charging system, ignition switch and anti-theft system tested.

issues.t: Heat and A/C blow from the wrong vents or at the wrong temperature
issues.sym: Air comes out of the wrong vents, the temperature won't change, or you hear clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: Small electric motors called door actuators move the flaps that direct air and blend hot and cold. They wear out on these cars.
issues.next: Listen for clicking behind the dash when you change settings. Replacing the failed actuator fixes it; some are easy to reach and others take more labor.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for warm air from the A/C, and owners report A/C compressor failures.
issues.next: Have the A/C system pressures checked and leak-tested. A failed compressor or a leak is the usual cause.

issues.t: Airbag or seat belt warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag or seat belt warning light stays on, or a seat belt buckle sticks.
issues.why: Owners report these lights staying on at higher mileage. GM issued a bulletin for sticking seat belt buckles that turn the warning light on.
issues.next: Have the airbag system codes read. The airbags may not work properly while the light is on, so get it fixed.

issues.t: Clunk from the steering when turning
issues.sym: A clunk you hear or feel in the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: GM issued many bulletins for this clunk, traced to the intermediate steering shaft between the column and the steering gear.
issues.next: Have the steering checked to rule out worn tie rods or mounts. A lubricated or replacement intermediate shaft usually fixes the noise.

issues.t: Misfire or rough idle from fuel injector problems
issues.sym: A check engine light, a rough idle, hesitation or chugging, or a hard start.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for misfires caused by corrosion at the fuel injector connections and by clogged injectors.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Cleaning or replacing injectors, or repairing the injector wiring, fixes most cases.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pan or rear main seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine, a burning oil smell, or the oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for repeat oil pan gasket leaks and released a new rear main seal for the 3.8L.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the leak traced. An oil pan gasket is a moderate job; a rear main seal takes much more labor.

issues.t: Harsh clunk into drive or reverse when cold
issues.sym: A hard clunk or jolt when shifting into drive or reverse on a cold morning.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for harsh garage shifts on cold starts in the 4-speed automatic.
issues.next: Mention it to a shop at your next service so they can check the fluid and apply any bulletin fix.

issues.t: Rusted floor under the rear-seat battery
issues.sym: Corrosion or holes in the floor pan around the battery under the rear seat, or a damp smell.
issues.why: The battery sits under the rear seat on these cars. Acid fumes and moisture can corrode the floor around it, and GM issued bulletins about it.
issues.next: When replacing the battery, look for rust and make sure the vent tube is attached. Repair rust early before it spreads.

issues.t: Whine or hum from the alternator in the cabin
issues.sym: A whine or hum you hear inside the car at idle and low speeds, sometimes through the speakers.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for alternator (generator) whine reaching the cabin.
issues.next: Have the alternator and its output tested. If it is weak or noisy, replacing it usually stops the whine.

issues.t: Paint bubbling on the aluminum hood
issues.sym: Blisters, bubbles or corrosion under the paint on the hood.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for early corrosion and blistering on the aluminum hood.
issues.next: Have a body shop look at it. Small spots can be sanded and refinished; bad cases need a hood refinish or replacement.

issues.t: Paint peeling off the hood and roof
issues.sym: The clear coat and paint flake or peel off the hood, roof and other top surfaces.
issues.why: Owners of the 1998 model report the factory paint failing on surfaces that face the sun.
issues.next: Wash and wax often to slow it down. A lasting fix means sanding and repainting the affected panels.

issues.t: Tilt steering column sticks in one position
issues.sym: The tilt wheel won't release and stays stuck in the highest or another position.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for the tilt mechanism sticking in the steering column.
issues.next: Don't force it. A shop can repair the tilt mechanism in the column.

issues.t: Wrong spark plugs installed at the factory (campaign)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; some cars may run poorly or misfire.
issues.why: Some supercharged engines were built with the wrong spark plugs, so GM ran an emissions campaign to inspect and replace them.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the campaign was done on your VIN. If not, have the plugs checked and replaced with the correct type.

issues.t: Leaking fuel pressure regulator can cause a backfire and fire (recall)
issues.sym: A loud backfire when starting, a fuel smell, or hard starting.
issues.why: A leaking fuel pressure regulator can let fuel into the intake. A backfire can then crack the intake manifold, pull an injector loose, and cause a fuel leak and possible fire. GM recalled about 910,000 cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell fuel, don't start the engine. Ask a Pontiac or GM dealer whether the recall was completed on your VIN.

issues.t: Backfire can break the intake and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: The engine won't start after a backfire, or there is a fuel smell under the hood.
issues.why: A defect involving the intake manifold could keep the engine from starting and could lead to an engine compartment fire.
issues.next: Check with a GM dealer that this old recall was done. Have any fuel smell or backfire looked at right away.

issues.t: Key and seat belt reminder chimes may not sound (recall)
issues.sym: No chime when the key is left in the ignition or a seat belt is unbuckled.
issues.why: A fault in the ignition anti-theft system could keep the warning chimes from sounding.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the recall was done. Until then, check for the key and buckle up without relying on the chime.

issues.t: Gear indicator may not match the actual gear (recall)
issues.sym: The shift indicator shows a different gear than the one the transmission is in, so the car may go into reverse when you expect drive.
issues.why: A link in the shift system could come loose, so the indicator and the transmission no longer agree.
issues.next: If the car moves in a direction you don't expect, stop and have it towed. Ask a dealer whether the recall was done.

issues.t: Aluminum wheel may separate from the car (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, a wobble or a clunk from a wheel.
issues.why: On a small number of cars, the aluminum wheels could separate from the vehicle.
issues.next: If a wheel feels loose or wobbles, stop driving. Ask a dealer to check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: ABS and stability control unit may not work properly (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction or stability warning lights, or braking that feels unusual in hard stops.
issues.why: The brake hydraulic control unit could leak internally, so rear brake balance, ABS, traction control and stability control may not work as designed.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall and inspect the brake system.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can break apart (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign before a crash.
issues.why: The driver's airbag inflator could fracture when it deploys, throwing pieces at people inside and leaving the airbag only partly inflated.
issues.next: Check with a GM dealer that the airbag recall was done on your VIN.

issues.t: Fuel can leak during refueling (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell or wetness near the tank after filling up.
issues.why: Fuel system parts near the fuel tank pressure sensor could be damaged during refueling and leak fuel, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel after filling up, don't drive it. Ask a dealer whether the recall was done.
